# Deal Postmortem — Brand Kit

**Tagline:** *The deals behind the companies you know.*
**Promise:** Every episode dissects one acquisition, merger, or buyout: what was paid, how it was financed, what went right or wrong, and who got rich or hurt. Neutral, evidence-first, never activist.

## Assets (generated by `python brand/make_logo.py`)
| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `avatar_800.png` | channel profile picture (YouTube crops it to a circle; the mark stays inside) |
| `banner_2560x1440.png` | channel banner (text sits inside the 1546×423 safe area) |
| `watermark_150.png` | YouTube branding watermark (Studio → Customization → Branding) |

**The mark:** a price chart that climbs, spikes, crashes, then **flatlines in red**, like a heart monitor. Deal → hype → collapse → postmortem.

## Colors
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Paper | `#EDEAE3` | editorial backgrounds (Template A), banner |
| Ink | `#111111` | text, avatar background |
| Signal Red | `#C8102E` | underlines, arrows, the flatline, bottom bar. **The only accent on editorial pieces** |
| Deal Yellow | `#F2C230` | dollar figures on Template B only |
| Night | `#0E0E10` | dark backgrounds (Template B) |

## Type (all free for commercial use, SIL OFL; get them from fonts.google.com)
| Role | Font | Fallback used until installed |
|---|---|---|
| Headlines / editorial thumbnails | **DM Serif Display** | Georgia Bold |
| Collapse thumbnails / big numbers | **Anton** | Impact |
| On-screen captions, lower thirds, charts | **Inter** (Regular/Bold) | Arial |

To install: download the three families from Google Fonts and drop `DMSerifDisplay-Regular.ttf`, `Anton-Regular.ttf`, `Inter-Bold.ttf`, `Inter-Regular.ttf` into `brand/fonts/`. The thumbnail and logo scripts pick them up automatically. Re-run `make_logo.py` afterward.

## Thumbnail templates (`tools/thumbnails/make_thumb.py`)
- **A: Editorial** (default, ~70% of videos). Paper background, one hero object on the right (the victim brand's product or logo, **with the acquirer physically attached**: price tag, flag, puppet strings, shredder), 2–4 words of serif text on the left, one word underlined in red.
- **B: Collapse** (big-number disaster stories). Night background with a red glow, yellow dollar figure + red down-arrow, huge condensed white text, hero logo cracked or on fire.
- Rules: ≤ 4 words · the text adds emotion and doesn't repeat the title · one focal object · readable at 160 px wide · no AI-generated faces of real people · make 3 variants for every upload and A/B them with Test & Compare.

Samples: `tools/thumbnails/samples/`. The spec format is in the script's docstring.

## Voice and tone
- Narrator: the owner's own cloned voice. Calm, confident, a little dry. Think "the smartest person at the deal table explaining it over a drink."
- Explain the jargon the first time (LBO, sale-leaseback, write-down) in one plain sentence.
- Neutral: show the buyer's logic *and* the outcome. Let numbers make the case. Use "alleged" for anything litigated.
- Never: rage-bait, "they don't want you to know", or unsourced claims.

## Title style
Proven formulas from `RESEARCH.md`, adapted:
- "[Buyer] Paid $[X] for [Brand]. Then…"
- "The Company That Secretly Owns Your [X]"
- "[Brand] Wasn't Killed by [Popular Myth]"
- "How Private Equity Bought Every [X] in America"
- "The $[X] Deal Everyone Laughed At"
